source.title: Situating the default-mode network along a principal gradient of macroscale cortical organization
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

confidence_rationale: Strong empirical grounding (humans + macaque) that a transmodal integration hub (the DMN) sits at the apex of a principal cortical gradient, maximally and equidistantly removed from primary sensory/motor cortex -- exactly the topographical signature of a region whose function is to integrate information detached from immediate sensory input. This grounds the BIOLOGICAL plausibility of MECH-423's readiness condition R-DMN (a DMN-analogue offline integration hub). Confidence held to 0.66 because REE has no explicit DMN module (per project_attention_distributed_precision_selection, REE's analogue is distributed), so the mapping is to a FUNCTIONAL prerequisite, not a named substrate component.
failure_signatures: If the integrated substrate has no apex region detached from sensory/motor streams (no transmodal hub equidistant from the modalities it integrates), there is no locus for cross-module integration to occur -- integration collapses back to within-modality processing and the super-additive gap does not open.

The gradient is a structural/topographical observation; an integration hub being PRESENT does not entail it is actively integrating during the measurement window -- a static hub with no online integration is the degenerate-readiness case.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Decomposition of human and macaque connectivity yields a principal gradient anchored at one end by primary sensory/motor regions and at the other by transmodal cortex (the DMN); DMN regions lie at the greatest and precisely-equidistant geodesic distance from primary sensory/motor landmarks, positioning the DMN to process transmodal information unrelated to immediate sensory input.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the biological reality of MECH-423's DMN-analogue readiness condition: super-additive cross-model integration needs a locus that sits ABOVE the individual sensory/affordance streams and integrates them while detached from immediate input -- the offline/DMN-style integration the readiness gate requires. In REE this 'apex' is the shared L-space latent (ARC-004) plus its offline consolidation regime rather than a dedicated DMN module.
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE does not implement an explicit DMN; the project's standing position is that attention/integration is distributed (project_attention_distributed_precision_selection). So this paper supports the FUNCTIONAL necessity of an integration apex, not a one-to-one substrate mapping. It is also a structural connectivity result -- it shows the hub exists, not that it is integrating on any given trial.
mapping.source_context: Resting-state fMRI connectivity gradients in humans and macaque; macroscale cortical topography; transmodal vs unimodal hierarchy.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality cross-species empirical paper. Mapping fidelity lowered because the readiness condition it grounds (a DMN-analogue integration hub) is realised in REE as a distributed/latent property rather than a discrete module, and the result is topographical rather than a dynamic integration measurement. Transfer risk elevated for the same reason.
